title: Paella With Crunchy Socarrat
description:
Paella is so iconic that people around the world think of it as the quintessential Spanish dish, even though it’s actually more Valencian (Valencia is in Spain, though). The paella is all things good: juicy seasoned meats, tender-crisp peas (or other green veggies), and the best part, saffron scented rice with crispy toasty rice bits. It is a dream come true.
If you’re using Bomba rice in your paella, you’ll add three cups of liquid for every cup of raw rice. Italian Arborio rice is often used as a substitute for Bomba because Arborio is widely available. If you use this variety of rice, you’ll need to adjust the liquid, so that you’re using two cups of water or stock for every cup of rice. (The ratios here reflect the inclusion of the saffron water.)
ingredients: 20 threads saffron lightly crushed, about 1/2 tsp
a little neutral oil high heat such as grapeseed preferred
4-6 or more bone-in skin on chicken thighs
1 red or orange pepper sliced into 1" strips
2 medium tomatoes diced or grated, about 2 cups
3 cups chicken broth with Bomba / 2 cups with Arborio (see above)
1 cup Bomba or Arborio rice (see above)
1 cup or so peas (fresh or frozen thawed)
lemon slices and/or garlic mayo for serving (optional)
directions: Stir the saffron into ½ cup hot chicken broth in a small bowl and let bloom while you prepare the chicken and vegetables.

In a good size paella pan (or similar), heat a little oil over medium-high heat. Sprinkle the chicken with salt and paprika, then cook, skin side down, until browned, about 5-7 minutes. Flip the chicken over and cook for another 3 minutes. Set aside.
Use the juiced pan to cook the onions, peppers, garlic, tomatoes, with a little more salt and pepper and paprika (all this the sofrito), stirring often, until the mix softens, about 5 minutes.
Add the chorizo, saffron water, and 1½ cups of chicken stock for Bomba rice or ¾ cup for Arborio. Bring everything to a boil over high heat.

Sprinkle in the rice, distributing evenly, then nestle in the chicken. Cook, uncovered, over medium heat, without stirring, until rice has absorbed most of the liquid, about 12-15 minutes. If the pan is larger than the burner, rotate it every two minutes to evenly distribute the heat. Once the stock is low enough, add the remaining chicken stock – 1 cup for Bomba, ¾ cup for Arborio.
Reduce heat to low, and top with the peas (and/or shrimp). Continue to cook, without covering or stirring, until the rice absorbs the liquid and is al dente, 5–10 minutes more.
Turn heat to high for 1-2 minutes to create the socarrat. Remove pan from heat, cover with a towel or aluminum foil, and let sit for 5 minutes before enjoying.
